description:
Final wiring step: make the default conversation repo template surface dispatch + await as worker-callable tools, so a fresh 'lernie new' repo can dispatch subagents end-to-end without per-repo customization (ARCH §4.3 — roles.<role>.tools selects from the on-disk pool).

Scope:
- Update template/providers.yaml roles.worker.tools to include dispatch and await alongside existing v0.3 entries (bash, read_file).
- Verify the tools list is correctly surfaced into the model call's tools: [...] array via the existing v0.3 tool-list-assembly path. dispatch and await SKILL.md descriptions and JSON schemas (from Phases 2-3) get composed in.
- Update template/souls/worker.md if a soul-level callout for dispatch/await is needed (subagent dispatch is a non-obvious capability; agents may need a hint).
- A scaffold-then-prompt scratch run drives the worker to emit a dispatch tool_use, the subagent runs and merges, the worker then emits await, the parent terminates and merges to main.

Out of scope:
- Workflow.yaml event hooks (worker_return, etc) — v0.6.
- A 'parser' role in the default template (folded into Phase 6 if that phase needed it).

Tests:
- Template loader test asserts the worker tools list contains dispatch and await.
- Integration end-to-end: lernie new + lernie prompt drives a dispatch with a fake adapter that emits the right tool_use sequence; subagent runs and merges; result returned to parent.

Done-when: a fresh 'lernie new' repo produces a worker role that can dispatch subagents without further customization, demonstrated by the integration test.
title: v0.4 Phase 7: default worker tools list includes dispatch + await
